title: Harden 2 timing-fragile e2e tests that false-positive the plan preflight under full-suite CPU load
description:
The plan-runner preflight runs the full `bun test` suite. Under heavy CPU load (e.g. a full-suite run inside a live `cam run` session, or a loaded dev machine) two timing-fragile e2e tests intermittently fail, wedging every plan preflight with a false-positive:

1. test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts:223 — 'recycle watcher e2e: arming marker SIGTERMs fake-claude; bash wrapper respawns with new UUID' (respawn-timing assertion race).
2. test/interactivity/interactivity.test.ts Test 5 — 'runInit ... does not throw and exits via the linear print path' (hard 5000ms timeout, exceeded under load).

Evidence (2026-07-16): both pass in isolation (2.7s / 1.3s) and passed CI on the CAM-311 merge; a full-suite run under contention took 116s with these 2 failing, while a quiet-machine re-run took 54s with 4603 pass / 0 fail. So the tests are logically correct but load-sensitive. They violate the project's own async-wait invariant ('poll with waitForCondition, never fixed setTimeout').

Fix: replace the fixed timing budgets with waitForCondition polling and/or explicit generous per-test timeouts on these two subprocess-spawning e2e tests so the preflight cannot false-positive under load. Impact: preflight false-positives silently block the autonomous drain (observed this session; recovered by re-running when the machine was quiet).

spec.scope: Replace the fixed timing budgets in two subprocess-spawning e2e tests so the plan-runner preflight full-suite `bun test` run cannot false-positive under CPU contention. Targets: test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts:223 (recycle-watcher respawn-timing race) and test/interactivity/interactivity.test.ts Test 5 (runInit linear-print path, hard 5000ms timeout). Test-only change; no product source modified.
acceptanceCriteria: The orch-recycle-watch respawn assertion uses waitForCondition polling instead of a fixed setTimeout/timing budget, conforming to the project 'poll with waitForCondition, never fixed setTimeout' invariant.
interactivity.test.ts Test 5 has an explicit generous per-test timeout (or polling) so it does not exceed its budget under full-suite CPU contention.
Both tests pass in isolation and under a full-suite `bun test` run; no product source files are modified (only the two named test files).
gotchas: The two tests are logically correct and pass in isolation (2.7s/1.3s) and in CI; the failure is purely load-sensitive timing. Do not weaken assertion correctness, only timing sensitivity.
A preflight false-positive silently blocks the autonomous drain, so the fix must hold under contention, not only on a quiet machine.
